public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in AI & Compute

data.narrative:
Core Automation, a stealth-stage AI & Software company founded by Gerald Depew and Daniel C. Rozok, is pursuing a Series funding round targeting $500M–$1B at a $4–5B+ post-money valuation. The relevant comp universe consists of one public peer (Palantir, ticker PLTR) and eight private AI & Software companies, including Figure AI, Scale AI, Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition.

Standard peer-median valuation proved inapplicable due to insufficient narrow comparables. While 12 same-sector peers exist in the AI & Software category, none of the filtered subsets—same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier—yielded three or more datapoints necessary for robust median analysis. Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given the heterogeneity of AI & Software valuations at different development and commercialization stages.

The stated fundraising target of $4–5B+ valuation reflects the founders' expectation within the frontier-tech AI space but lacks quantitative validation from comparable transaction data. Key uncertainties include the company's actual stage of product-market fit, revenue or customer traction (not disclosed), and how the private comp set's recent valuations map to current market conditions. A credible valuation range cannot be triangulated without either meaningful operating metrics or access to tighter peer datasets.
